chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad, from Rabi', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon him), regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'Then let them end their impurity'.
The hair surrounding the man's body (from shaving/perfuming).

key_terms.تَفَثَهُمْ: Their impurity (specifically referring to shaved hair in this context)
key_terms.مَحُفُوفُ: Surrounded or encompassing (referring to the hair)

ai.seo_question: What does 'tafath' refer to in the context of Hajj rituals according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Istibsar*, the Imams interpret 'tafath' in Surah Al-Hajj not merely as general impurity, but specifically as the hair removed during Hajj, which is then perfumed to signify the transition from the state of Ihram to a state of purity and honor. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the physical and spiritual cleanliness associated with ritual acts, linking the removal of hair (a symbol of humility) with the application of scent (a symbol of dignity).
